Every brelkid, a newly described family.why: The brelkids are made up: a family of vertebrates of that name does not exist, and no text states this. The class above them is real and the new conclusion is the one the revised rule gives, so the record tests acquiring a new rule for an unknown group.

The heart of Pelka has three chambers..why: Made up, so stated nowhere: nobody writes a fact about an animal that does not exist. It follows only from the inserted rule and the membership given in the prompt (the individual is named as a brelkid), which is how people state things about a member of a group: through its group.

A brelkid has the same number of heart c.why: Nobody compares the heart of a made-up family of vertebrates with that of frogs. What people do say is that a frog has a three-chambered heart; the comparison follows only from the inserted rule and that fact.

notes: TBox expansion paired with biology-replace-0007 (mammal heart: four chambers to three): keeps the revision's relation and new object (three chambers) and gives it to a made-up family of vertebrates (the brelkids) under the real class 'vertebrate', which leaves the number of heart chambers open (two in fish, three in amphibians, four in birds and mammals), so no inherited rule is overridden and the old value has nothing to push out. Own questions ask the new value; the propositional side facts are one true and one false. Derived: an inheritance question and an application that name a member in the prompt, and a composition that compares with a fact stored about frogs, whose three-chambered heart is stored (derivation none). Unrelated near: a dog's heart (four), so a leak of the rule onto real members would change it. Placed under a real class that leaves the property open, so the insert fills an empty slot and overwrites nothing (no overwriting, README Expansion).
